questions.text: What happens if a CPD provider's accreditation expires without renewal?

options.text: Automatic extension for one additional year, provided certain conditions are met
Activities delivered lose accreditation; no valid CPD credits generated
Credits are valid for one year after expiration, allowing time for renewal
The provider is immediately re-accredited, assuming no violations occurred

rationale.a: Incorrectly grants automatic grace period; re-accreditation must be applied for before expiration.
rationale.c: Falsely extends validity; accreditation expiration terminates credit validity immediately.
rationale.d: Contradicts the requirement for application and evaluation; re-accreditation is not automatic.
rationale.correct: After accreditation expiration without renewal, activities delivered do not generate valid CPD credits; architects cannot claim credit from expired providers.
rationale.takeaway: CPD credits from providers become invalid immediately upon accreditation expiration—no grace period applies.

questions.explanation: Incorrectly grants automatic grace period; re-accreditation must be applied for before expiration. Falsely extends validity; accreditation expiration terminates credit validity immediately. Contradicts the requirement for application and evaluation; re-accreditation is not automatic. After accreditation expiration without renewal, activities delivered do not generate valid CPD credits; architects cannot claim credit from expired providers. CPD credits from providers become invalid immediately upon accreditation expiration—no grace period applies.

questions.text: What is the architect's responsibility regarding CPD provider selection?

options.text: Architects can enroll in any program and claim CPD credit, regardless of the provider's accreditation status.
Architects must verify provider accreditation status before enrolling
The Board automatically notifies architects of approved providers, ensuring compliance with CPD requirements.
All programs count equally regardless of provider status, simplifying the selection process for architects.

rationale.a: Fails to apply the accreditation requirement; non-accredited programs generate no CPD credit.
rationale.c: Reverses the responsibility; architects must proactively verify, not wait for Board notifications.
rationale.d: Ignores the accreditation distinction; credits are valid only from accredited providers.
rationale.correct: Architects must verify provider accreditation status before enrollment; only credits from accredited providers count toward the mandatory 45-unit requirement.
rationale.takeaway: Architects are responsible for verifying provider accreditation before enrollment to ensure CPD credit validity.

questions.text: Which organization holds authority to accredit CPD providers for architects?

options.text: The Professional Regulation Commission exclusively
The Board of Architecture
Individual professional organizations
International architectural associations

rationale.a: Misidentifies the PRC as sole authority; the Board of Architecture, not the PRC, accredits providers.
rationale.c: Incorrectly distributes authority to individual organizations; only the Board holds accreditation authority.
rationale.d: Assigns authority to foreign entities; accreditation is a domestic regulatory function.
rationale.correct: The CPD Council for Architecture (under the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture) accredits CPD providers.
rationale.takeaway: The CPD Council for Architecture holds authority to accredit CPD providers.

questions.text: What does the Board evaluate when accrediting CPD providers?

options.text: Only the provider's size and location, focusing on the physical capacity to host participants and the geographical accessibility
Instructor qualifications, curriculum content, facilities, and teaching methodologies
Only the provider's registration with the SEC, ensuring legal compliance and operational legitimacy
Provider age and years in business, considering the historical performance and experience in delivering educational programs

rationale.a: Ignores quality criteria; size and location do not determine educational quality.
rationale.c: Confuses business registration with educational accreditation; SEC registration does not substitute for quality evaluation.
rationale.d: Relies on irrelevant factors; longevity in business does not guarantee current instructional quality.
rationale.correct: The Board evaluates instructor qualifications, curriculum design, course content, learning outcomes, facilities, and instructional methodologies during accreditation review.
rationale.takeaway: Accreditation evaluation focuses on instructor expertise, curriculum design, and instructional quality—not business registration or age.

questions.text: When an architectural firm collaborates with multiple providers to deliver a CPD program, what must be verified?

options.text: Only the lead firm's accreditation status, which may not cover all aspects of the program
Accreditation status of all participating providers
Only participant enrollment numbers, which do not affect the program's accreditation
Only the course topic relevance, which is important but not sufficient for accreditation

rationale.a: Incorrectly permits non-accredited co-providers; accreditation must apply to all partners.
rationale.c: Ignores accreditation status entirely; enrollment numbers do not determine credit validity.
rationale.d: Confuses content relevance with accreditation; both are required, but accreditation is essential for credit validity.
rationale.correct: When organizations collaborate on CPD programs, all co-offering organizations must hold accreditation status; credits are only valid if all participating providers are accredited.
rationale.takeaway: All participating providers in a collaborative CPD program must be accredited; a single non-accredited partner invalidates credits.

questions.text: How does automatic accreditation of the professional organization differ from other providers?

options.text: The professional organization has less stringent quality requirements compared to independently accredited CPD providers
The professional organization is not required to apply; other providers must undergo evaluation
The professional organization pays lower accreditation fees than independent CPD training providers
All organizations receive automatic accreditation equally regardless of their affiliation or organizational type

rationale.a: Falsely suggests lower standards; automatic accreditation reflects the organization's central regulatory role, not reduced quality expectations.
rationale.b: Remove or correct self-referential explanation for correct option.
rationale.c: Incorrectly focuses on fees; the distinction is procedural (automatic vs. applied), not financial.
rationale.d: Denies UAP's unique automatic status; the professional organization is the sole recipient of automatic accreditation.
rationale.correct: Only the integrated accredited professional organization receives automatic accreditation without separate application; other providers must undergo standard evaluation.
rationale.takeaway: UAP alone receives automatic accreditation; all other providers must apply and undergo Board evaluation.

questions.text: Which professional organization is automatically accredited as a CPD provider?

options.text: All architectural associations equally, regardless of their specific focus or membership size
The United Architects of the Philippines, Inc. (UAP)
Regional architectural chapters, provided they meet certain membership thresholds and activity levels
International architectural organizations only, if they have a recognized presence in the Philippines

rationale.a: Falsely grants automatic accreditation to all associations; only UAP receives automatic status.
rationale.c: Incorrectly attributes automatic status to regional chapters; automatic accreditation applies only to the national integrated organization.
rationale.d: Restricts automatic status to foreign entities; automatic accreditation is reserved for the Philippine integrated organization.
rationale.correct: The United Architects of the Philippines (UAP), as the Accredited Integrated Professional Organization (AIPO) is automatically accredited as a CPD provider without requiring separate application.
rationale.takeaway: UAP (United Architects of the Philippines) holds automatic CPD provider accreditation—no separate application required.

questions.text: What is the consequence of completing CPD activities from a non-accredited provider?

options.text: Credits count if the content is relevant to architectural practice and approved by a recognized authority
Credits count but at half the normal credit value, subject to verification by the accrediting body
No valid CPD credits are generated regardless of content quality
Credits are valid for one renewal cycle only, provided they meet the minimum standards set by the board

rationale.a: Falsely permits credit based on content relevance; accreditation status, not content alone, determines validity.
rationale.b: Incorrectly grants partial credit; the all-or-nothing rule applies—no credits without accreditation.
rationale.d: Falsely extends validity to one cycle; non-accredited provider credits are never valid.
rationale.correct: Non-accredited provider activities generate no valid CPD credits regardless of content quality, time invested, or architectural relevance.
rationale.takeaway: Non-accredited provider activities generate zero valid CPD credits, regardless of content quality.

questions.text: What is the validity period for CPD provider accreditation?

options.text: One year from issuance
Two years from issuance
Three years from issuance
Five years from issuance

rationale.a: Overly short duration; annual re-accreditation would impose excessive administrative burden.
rationale.b: Undercounts the validity period; actual term is three years, not two.
rationale.d: Overcounts; five years exceeds the three-year accreditation validity.
rationale.correct: CPD provider accreditation is valid for three years from issuance; providers must apply for re-accreditation before expiration.
rationale.takeaway: CPD provider accreditation is valid for three years and requires re-accreditation before expiration.

questions.explanation: Overly short duration; annual re-accreditation would impose excessive administrative burden. Undercounts the validity period; actual term is three years, not two. CPD provider accreditation is valid for three years and requires re-accreditation before expiration.

questions.text: What minimum standards must accredited providers meet regarding course design?

options.text: No specific standards are required, allowing for flexibility in course content and delivery methods
Clearly defined learning outcomes aligned with professional track categories
Only that courses are led by licensed architects, ensuring professional oversight and expertise
Only that certificates are issued to participants, which serves as proof of attendance and completion

rationale.a: Ignores quality standards; the Board prescribes detailed design requirements.
rationale.c: Limits requirements to instructors; course design standards go beyond instructor licensing.
rationale.d: Confuses certificates with course design; certificate issuance is an output, not a design standard.
rationale.correct: Accredited providers must have clearly defined learning objectives aligned with professional track categories and assessment methods evaluating participant competency acquisition.
rationale.takeaway: Accredited providers must have clearly defined learning outcomes aligned with the five professional track categories.
